headline: Showers end tonight, then a cold, dry weekend with frost and freezing lows early Saturday and mostly dry weather into next week.
summary: Leftover showers from a weakening low-pressure system high in the atmosphere fade this evening as it moves south. Highs have been in the low to mid 50s, and the weekend stays dry and cool with afternoon highs in the low 50s. Trick-or-treaters should have dry weather, but it will be cold. The coldest stretch is early Saturday morning, when skies clear and winds go light. A Freeze Warning, from midnight tonight to 9 AM Saturday, covers the lowlands of Lewis and southern Thurston Counties and the Middle Chehalis River Valley, where lows are expected in the upper 20s to low 30s. A Frost Advisory for the same hours covers the northern Olympic Peninsula and areas north of Seattle, including the Eastside, Everett, Marysville, Shoreline, Lynnwood, eastern Kitsap County, and the western Skagit and Whatcom lowlands, with temperatures of 32 to 36 expected. Forecasters advise protecting sensitive plants. Sunday morning lows will again be near freezing, in the low 30s. A ridge of high pressure (a zone of sinking, settled air) keeps things mostly dry into the first half of next week. A few weak disturbances could bring light rain chances west of Puget Sound early in the week and around midweek. A stronger front later in the week looks more likely to change the pattern, but forecasters say the details are quite uncertain because computer model runs increasingly disagree.
changes: Through the day, the freeze threat went from a Freeze Watch to a Freeze Warning, and the evening discussion added a Frost Advisory for areas north of Seattle and the northern Olympic Peninsula. Next week's outlook shifted from a Thursday chance of rain to a stronger front late in the week with low confidence.
